note.question: How should local content requirements under technology gaps be optimized?
note.overview: This paper studies how the government of a developing country optimizes its local content requirement (LCR) policy to maximize social welfare in a setting where foreign original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) produce and sell multicomponent products in the developing country. The foreign OEMs’ local sourcing of components is more costly than global sourcing because of technology gaps between local and global suppliers. We characterize and compare the optimal product-level and component-level LCR policies imposed on multicomponent products.
